sentences.text: Per: Justice Vivek Rusia This petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been filed by the petitioner being aggrieved by the orders dated 18.08.2022 and 18.10.2022 passed by the respondent No. 3 seeking direction to refer the matter to the competent civil court under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act of 1956').
02. As per the facts of the case, Baniya was the owner of agricultural land bearing survey nos. 169 and 92/1 situated at village Katghara, District Khargone.
After his death in 1997, the aforesaid land were mutated in the name of his legal heirs namely Maru Bai (wife), Gopal (son), Chunnilal
NEUTRAL

CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:31564 2 WP-8944-2023 (son), Mangri Bai (daughter)
and Basu Bai (daughter/present petitioner).
Petitioner has filed the copy of revenue records as Annexure P/4.
According to the petitioner, Gopal and Chunnilal sold their respective shares vide sale deed dated 01.02.1997 in favour of Smt. Savitri Bai who is the mother of Rohit Khaitan-respondent No.4.
Thereafter, the name of Savitri Bai was mutated in respect of the entire land bearing survey nos. 169 and 92/1.
After the death of Savitri Bai, name of respondent No.4-Rohit Khaitan was mutated in the revenue records.

sentences.text: Authority of India (NHAI) acquired the land bearing survey no. 169 for construction of four lane highway and compensation of Rs. 30,46,000/- payable to respondent No.4 was determined.

Petitioner moved an objection claiming the compensation to the extent of her share in the land bearing survey no. 169 and 92/1, but the same has been rejected vide impugned orders dated 18.08.2022 and 18.10.2022.
According to the petitioner, being co-owner of the land bearing survey No. 169 and 92/1, she is also entitled to get compensation to the extent of her share.
Petitioner filed an application under Section 3 of the Act of 1956 seeking reference of the dispute to the civil court which has also been rejected, hence this petition before this Court.

03. Shri Baheti, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that there is a dispute between the petitioner and respondent No.4 pertaining to apportionment of the compensation as they are co-owners of the land, therefore the competent authority is bound to refer the dispute under Section 3H(4) of the Act of 1956 to the principal civil court of original jurisdiction.
Petitioner has no other r e m e d y b u t t o a p p r o a c h t h e c i v i l c o u r t b y w a y o f N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2024:MPHC-IND:31564 3 WP-8944-2023 reference under Section 3H(4) of the Act of 1956.
Therefore, the impugned orders be set aside and the respondents be directed to refer the dispute to the civil court.

04. Ms. Anita Sharma, learned counsel for the respondent No.2- NHAI submits that the land bearing survey nos. 169 and 92/1 situated at village Katghara, District Khargone were found to be mutated in the name of Savitri Bai - mother of respondent No.4 at the time of issuance of the notification under Section 3A dated 20.11.2019 and publication under Section 3D dated 02.11.2020 hence, the competent authority passed the award for payment of compensation to the tune of

Rs.
2,17,367/- for survey no. 92/1 and Rs. 19,34,391/- for survey no. 169
in favour of respondent No.4

. 
The brothers of the petitioner namely Gopal and Chunnilal had sold the land bearing survey no. 169 and 92/1 to Savitri Bai and therefore, the same was mutated in her name.
After the death of Savitri Bai, name of respondent No.4-Rohit Khaitan was mutated vide order dated 30.03.2022 in the revenue record which has not been challenged by the petitioner.
Therefore, the NHAI has not committed illegality while passing the award in favour of respondent No.4.
If the petitioner is aggrieved by the sale deed or mutation in the name of mother of respondent No.4 or respondent No.4, she is having an alternative efficacious remedy of filing a civil suit.
05. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

06. It is not in dispute that vide sale deed dated 01.02.1997, Gopal and Chunnilal sold the land bearing survey nos. 169 and 92/1 to Smt. Savitri Bai and accordingly, her name was mutated in the revenue records.
After her NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:31564 4 WP-8944-2023 death, name of respondent No.4-Rohit Khaitan has been mutated in the revenue records.
Based on the entries of the revenue record as well as the sale deed, the Sub Divisional Officer and the Land Acquisition Officer/competent officer rightly passed the award.

At the time of passing of the award,
no such objection was raised by the petitioner, therefore there was no occasion for the Land Acquisition Officer to decide the issue of apportionment.
The petitioner has raised objection before the Sub Divisional Officer at the time of disbursement of the compensation i.e. after passing of the award dated 01.06.2021.

Section 3H of the Act of 1956 is reproduced below :
''3H.
Deposit
and payment of amount

. --(1) The amount determined under section 3G shall be deposited by the Central Government in such manner as may be laid down by rules made in this behalf by that Government, with the competent authority before taking possession of the land.

(2) As soon as may be after the amount has been deposited under sub-section (1), the competent authority shall on behalf of the Central Government pay the amount to the person or persons entitled thereto.

(3) Where several persons claim to be interested in the amount deposited under sub- section (1), the competent authority shall determine the persons who in its opinion are entitled to receive the amount payable to each of them.

(4) If any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority shall refer the 5 dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.

(5) Where the amount determined under section 3G by the arbitrator is in excess of the amount determined by the competent authority, the arbitrator may award interest at nine per cent, per annum on such excess amount from the date of taking possession under section 3D till the date of the actual deposit thereof.

(6)Where the amount determined by the arbitrator is in excess of the amount determined by the competent authority, the excess amount together with interest, if any,
awarded under sub-section (5) shall be deposited by the Central Government in such manner as may be laid down by rules made in this behalf by that Government, with the competent authority and the provisions of subsections (2) to (4) shall apply to such deposit.''

08. As per sub-section (1) of Section 3H, the amount determined NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:31564 5 WP-8944-2023 under Section 3G shall be deposited by the Central Government with the competent authority before taking possession of the land.
Under sub-section (2), the competent authority shall on behalf of the Central Government pay the amount to the person or persons entitled thereto.

Where several persons claim to be interested in the amount deposited under sub-section (1), the competent authority shall determine the persons who in its opinion are entitled to receive the amount payable to each of them.
Sub- section

( 4) , if any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount of any part thereof or to any person whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority shall refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.

As per sub-section (2) of Section 3G, where the right of user or any right in the nature of an easement on, any land acquired under this Act, there shall be paid an amount to the owner or any other person whose right of enjoyment on that land has been affected in any manner.

After publication of notice by the competent authority, all the persons interested in such land may appear in person or by an agent or by a legal practitioner before the competent authority as has been provided under sub-section (4) of Section 3G of the Act of 1956.

sentences.text:
Therefore, the 'person' referred to in Section 3H are the person(s) who has a right to use or any right in the nature of easement or owner as explained in Section 3G(2), can raise an objection under Section 3G(4) and thereafter under sub-section (3) of Section 3H of the Act of 1956 before the competent authority who shall determine the entitlement to receive the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:31564 6 WP-8944-2023 amount payable to them.
10.

In the present case, petitioner is alleging that she has share in the land bearing survey nos. 169 &
92/1 which had been sold by Gopal and Chunnilal therefore, the sale deed is not binding on her.
The competent authority under the Act of 1956 is not the competent forum to declare the sale deed void and direct for distribution of the amount between the petitioner and respondent No.4.

The petitioner is required to challenge the sale deed as well as the order of mutation of respondent No.4 in the revenue records and if succeeds, thereafter she shall be entitled to claim her share in the amount of compensation.
For the aforesaid relief, petitioner is having the remedy of filing an appeal against the order of mutation as well as a civil suit for declaration of the sale deed as void.
In the said civil suit, petitioner may claim the amount of compensation to the extent of her share from respondent No.4 by impleading him as a defendant.
11. With the aforesaid liberty, this petition stands disposed of.
(VIVEK RUSIA)
